short_description: Slow checkout while the cache was down
trigger: Node drain for a kernel upgrade
problem_statement: The cache pod was evicted during a node drain and did not come back on its own. orders-api fell back to the database for every read, and checkout p95 latency rose to 2.8 seconds for 22 minutes.
impact_description: Checkout p95 latency rose from 250 ms to 2.8 s and orders-api logged connection refused errors for cache:6379.
impact_metrics: Checkout p95 latency rose to 2.8 seconds for 22 minutes (from 250 ms)
immediate_resolution: Node back in the cluster. Restarted the cache statefulset.

timeline.event: Node drain started for a kernel upgrade. Planned maintenance.
Cache pod evicted. orders-api logged connection refused errors for cache:6379. None.
Alert OrdersApiHighLatency fired. On-call opened an incident.
Cache pod found stuck in Pending, its volume bound to the drained node. Asked the platform on-call to bring the node back.
Node back in the cluster. Restarted the cache statefulset.
Latency back to normal. Closed the incident.

root_causes: The cache ran as a single pod with no PodDisruptionBudget, so a planned drain took it down.
Its volume was bound to one node, so the pod could not move to another node.

action_items.action: Add a PodDisruptionBudget for the cache.
Alert when redis-cli ping fails for 2 minutes.
